title: Translunar injection sends Orion toward the Moon
summary: NASA reported completion of the translunar injection burn, beginning Orion's journey from high Earth orbit toward the Moon.
source_title: Artemis II Flight Day 2: Orion Completes TLI Burn, Crew Begins Journey to the Moon
limitations: Timestamp is a Phase 0 placeholder at date-level precision and will be replaced by validated event time during Phase 1.

title: Crew and Mission Control troubleshoot Orion toilet fault
summary: NASA reported a fault indication associated with Orion's toilet. The crew and Mission Control worked the issue and restored the system to normal operation.
source_title: Artemis II Flight Update: Crew and Ground Teams Successfully Troubleshoot Orion's Toilet

decision_thread.detection: Fault indication observed for the waste-management system.
decision_thread.evidence: NASA publicly reported crew/ground troubleshooting and subsequent recovery.
decision_thread.constraint: Maintain crew-system functionality while preserving mission timeline and safety.
decision_thread.decision: Troubleshoot with Mission Control using available procedures.
decision_thread.action: Crew and ground team performed troubleshooting steps.
decision_thread.outcome: NASA reported the toilet returned to normal operation.

limitations: This record summarizes NASA's public report and does not claim access to internal procedures or telemetry.

title: Outbound trajectory correction burn cancelled
summary: NASA reported that a planned outbound trajectory correction was not needed because Orion remained on the intended path.
source_title: Artemis II Flight Day 3: Outbound Trajectory Correction Burn Update

decision_thread.detection: Navigation solution indicated Orion remained acceptably on trajectory.
decision_thread.evidence: NASA reported the planned correction was unnecessary.
decision_thread.constraint: Maintain the required lunar-return trajectory without unnecessary maneuvering.
options: Cancel correction if navigation criteria are satisfied
decision_thread.decision: Do not execute the planned correction.
decision_thread.outcome: Orion continued on the intended outbound trajectory.

limitations: Phase 0 uses NASA's public narrative; project does not yet reproduce the navigation criteria that drove the real decision.

title: Wastewater vent issue changes spacecraft attitude priorities
summary: NASA reported another trajectory correction was unnecessary. Controllers used spacecraft attitude and heating to support efforts to clear a suspected wastewater vent obstruction while the toilet remained operational.
source_title: Artemis II Flight Day 4: Deep Space Flying, Lunar Flyby Prep

decision_thread.detection: Public mission reporting described a suspected obstruction/ice concern in a wastewater vent line.
decision_thread.evidence: A trajectory correction was not required, making spacecraft attitude available for troubleshooting priorities.
decision_thread.constraint: Support waste-system operation without compromising required trajectory/vehicle constraints.
options: Use attitude/thermal conditions to support vent clearing
decision_thread.decision: Use spacecraft attitude and heating to support efforts to clear the vent.
decision_thread.action: Controllers pointed the relevant area toward the Sun and used heaters as reported by NASA.
decision_thread.outcome: NASA reported the toilet remained operational and backup waste collection capability was available.

limitations: No internal telemetry or exact flight-rule thresholds are represented.

title: Crewed lunar flyby and science observations
summary: Orion flew around the lunar farside on a free-return trajectory. The science campaign included targeted imaging and crew observations later released through the Planetary Data System.
source_title: Artemis II Preliminary Lunar Science Report and PDS Mission Archive
limitations: Exact closest-approach time and synchronized observation products will be ingested and validated in later phases.

title: Crew reports faint lunar impact flashes
summary: NASA's preliminary science report says the crew observed five extremely faint flashes during the lunar eclipse. Scientists evaluated alternative explanations before identifying them as lunar impact flashes.
source_title: Artemis II Preliminary Lunar Science Report

decision_thread.detection: Astronauts visually reported faint flashes on the lunar surface during eclipse conditions.
decision_thread.evidence: Crew reports, observation geometry, and later science analysis were compared.
decision_thread.constraint: Alternative explanations such as reflections or particle effects had to be considered.
decision_thread.decision: Science analysis favored lunar impact flashes after alternatives were evaluated.
decision_thread.action: Observations were documented and included in postflight science analysis.
decision_thread.outcome: NASA reported five faint lunar impact flashes.

limitations: Future phases should connect the report to precise PDS audio, annotations, imagery, and observation geometry.

title: Unexpected return-link loss ahead of correction burn
summary: NASA reported an unexpected loss of the return link during a data-rate change roughly two hours before a planned return trajectory correction burn. The event affected communications and telemetry; two-way communications were restored and burn preparations resumed.
source_title: Artemis II Flight Day 9: Second Return Correction Burn Complete

decision_thread.detection: Unexpected return-link loss occurred during a data-rate change.
decision_thread.evidence: NASA reported communications and telemetry were affected shortly before a planned maneuver.
decision_thread.constraint: Re-establish situational awareness and communications in time to safely continue maneuver preparation.
decision_thread.decision: Recover two-way communications before resuming maneuver preparation.
decision_thread.action: Ground teams restored communications and telemetry flow.
decision_thread.outcome: Burn preparations resumed and NASA later reported the second return correction burn complete.

limitations: The project does not yet include raw communications telemetry or internal recovery procedures.

title: Orion completes atmospheric entry and splashdown
summary: NASA's public entry coverage describes hypersonic atmospheric entry, a plasma communications blackout, parachute descent, and splashdown, closing the Artemis II flight.
source_title: Artemis II Flight Day 10: Re-entry Live Updates
limitations: Phase 0 summarizes public mission coverage. Entry-state reconstruction and modeled aerodynamic quantities belong in later phases.
